source.title: Cross-lingual Similarity of Multilingual Representations Revisited

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures cross-lingual representation similarity with multiple indexes and argues from its own results that index choice can change the conclusion. It also reports partial alignment patterns across multilingual models and scales.
record.gate_note: The study compares CKA, PWCCA, SVCCA, ANC, and sentence-matching accuracy for language representations within multilingual models. It does not compare independently trained models, vision and language models, or shared features across models. XNLI transfer scores are not included as rows because they measure task performance rather than representation similarity. Results cited from prior work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study compares representations of different languages inside a single multilingual model, not representations of independently trained models, modalities or seeds. It cites Li et al. (2015), one of the original sources, and says CKA/CCA suit cross-network comparison. Its metric-dependence result therefore concerns within-model cross-lingual similarity, a related but different construct, and does not test V6 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that CKA (and CCA, which has related problems) can miss cross-lingual similarity relevant to zero-shot transfer, and propose ANC for comparing languages within one model. With ANC they show the align-then-predict pattern generalizes to CLMs and to large MLMs and CLMs. They also state that CKA/CCA remain a good fit for comparing representations across different networks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies language representations within a single multilingual model and compares similarity indexes; it does not reproduce cross-model convergence methods. ANC assumes neurons are already aligned across languages.
record.method_sensitivity: The inferred deep-layer similarity changes with the index used (CKA versus ANC, PWCCA, or SVCCA). Language pair also varies across the plotted analyses. The paper does not report a systematic sensitivity analysis over input distributions.

fits_no_version.finding: In a Normformer XLM-R, CKA between language representations is near zero at layers 6-12. PWCCA/SVCCA give about 0.5-0.8, matching accuracy exceeds 50%, and ANC shows similarity; the CKA result repeats on a second seed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured cross-lingual similarity within a multilingual model depends strongly on the similarity index (CKA vs CCA variants vs neuron-wise correlation).

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-lingual ANC rises then partly falls with depth ('first align, then predict') in mBERT, XLM-R base to XXL (to 10.7B) and XGLM 564M to 7.5B. No increase of alignment with scale is claimed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The align-then-predict pattern of within-model cross-lingual similarity holds across MLM/CLM objectives and model sizes.

record.problems: The core comparisons are limited to selected language pairs and multilingual models; the paper says it did not test other language families or extremely low-resource languages. Many plotted values are not reported numerically in the text. The scaling results describe similarity trajectories but do not establish that similarity increases with model scale.
record.rows_left_out: The per-layer plotted values in Figures 3–9 are not exhaustively represented. For the scaling curves, only the first and last layer for each model are retained; intermediate layers are omitted because of the 60-row limit and are figure-only. Figures 1–4 and 7–9 also contain additional language-pair or layer points not itemized here.

untested.parts: No comparison between independently trained models. Scaling results are within-model cross-lingual trajectories.
Seeds are retrained but their representations are never compared.
No mapping, stitching or relative representations between models.
Metric dependence is shown only for within-model cross-lingual similarity, not for cross-model convergence.
No cross-model alignment levels and no causal analysis of shared data or objectives.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6/V7 links are rejected: every result concerns similarity between languages inside a single network, which the authors explicitly distinguish from cross-model comparison. The first/last-layer scaling rows are figure-only and carry no readable values.

versions.untested_parts: The scaling experiments measure language-to-language similarity within each multilingual model, not alignment between independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data, nor whether alignment rises with capability.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions are studied.
A second random initialization is used to check a CKA result, but the paper does not compare learned features or shared subspaces across seeds.
No mapping between models, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment is tested.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits across models are investigated.
Tests index choice and language-pair variation, but not neighbour-count settings or out-of-distribution inputs.
Reports incomplete align-then-predict patterns, but does not test whether shared data or objectives cause the alignment rather than a common model of reality.

rows.subject: scale_normformer (XLM-Roberta)
rows.operation_detail: Measured cross-lingual sentence-representation similarity with linear CKA.
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The paper says CKA drops dramatically at layer 6 and remains around zero in layers 6–12, despite cross-lingual transfer and matching evidence.
rows.check: Near-zero CKA is between English and French sentence representations within one model. This is cross-lingual similarity, not convergence between models.

rows.subject: scale_normformer (XLM-Roberta)
rows.operation_detail: Measured cross-lingual sentence-representation similarity with linear CKA.
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The paper describes layers 6–12 as hanging around zero on CKA.
rows.check: Same as R1: within-model cross-lingual CKA at layer 12.

rows.subject: scale_normformer (XLM-Roberta)
rows.operation_detail: Measured sentence-matching accuracy using cosine similarity to retrieve the parallel sentence.
rows.value: >50% for French across layers 6–12; the paper describes a slight decline
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The paper reports significant matching scores in deep layers, unlike CKA's near-zero result.
rows.check: Sentence-matching accuracy is within-model cross-lingual retrieval, not cross-model alignment.

rows.subject: scale_normformer (XLM-Roberta)
rows.operation_detail: Measured average neuron-wise correlation between language representations.
rows.value: figure only; the paper says ANC reveals cross-lingual similarity in deeper layers
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: Compared with CKA, ANC shows the align-then-predict pattern in deep Normformer layers.
rows.check: ANC requires neurons aligned a priori within one network, and the authors say it cannot compare different networks. The row also cites en-bg, but Figure 4 is described generally.

rows.subject: scale_normformer (XLM-Roberta)
rows.operation_detail: Measured similarity with PWCCA.
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The stated range contrasts with CKA's near-zero scores for the deep layers.
rows.check: PWCCA of about 0.5-0.8 is within-model cross-lingual similarity, not convergence between models.

rows.subject: scale_normformer (XLM-Roberta)

rows.uncertainty: not stated

rows.check: SVCCA of about 0.5-0.8 is within-model cross-lingual similarity, not convergence between models.

rows.subject: scale_normformer (XLM-Roberta)
rows.operation_detail: Measured cross-lingual sentence-representation similarity with linear CKA.
rows.value: figure only; the paper says CKA fails to reveal similarity in layers 6–11
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The last layer is CLS-pooled; the other layers are mean-pooled.
rows.check: Within-model cross-lingual CKA in the fine-tuned model; not cross-model.

rows.subject: scale_normformer (XLM-Roberta)
rows.operation_detail: Measured average neuron-wise correlation between language representations.
rows.value: figure only; the paper says ANC captures similarity across all layers
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The last layer is CLS-pooled; the other layers are mean-pooled.
rows.check: Within-model cross-lingual ANC in the fine-tuned model; not cross-model.

rows.subject: scale_normformer (XLM-Roberta), second random initialization
rows.operation_detail: Measured cross-lingual similarity with CKA after retraining from a different random initialization.
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The paper says the second initialization reproduces the deep-layer CKA result.
rows.check: The retrain only reproduces the within-model cross-lingual CKA result. The two seeds' representations are never compared with each other, so this does not bear on V3.

rows.subject: bert-base-multilingual-cased
rows.operation_detail: Measured average neuron-wise correlation between language representations.
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The paper says representations first align and then become somewhat language-specific again; the stated correlation at the most language-natural layers is about 0.7.
rows.check: ANC of about 0.7 measures language alignment within mBERT, not cross-model convergence. Its use as a sanity check makes it a validation of the study's own method.

rows.subject: bert-base-multilingual-cased
rows.operation_detail: Measured average neuron-wise correlation between language representations.
rows.value: figure only; the paper says the pattern is first align, then predict
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The paper describes convergence followed by slight divergence at deep layers.
rows.check: The align-then-predict trajectory over depth is within-model cross-lingual and is not V7's partial cross-model convergence.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: scale_normformer, especially deep layers; CKA compared with matching, ANC, PWCCA, and SVCCA
reader_labels.reason: CKA is around zero where sentence matching, ANC, PWCCA, and SVCCA indicate cross-lingual similarity (R1–R6). The paper also reports the same deep-layer CKA result after another initialization (R9).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports that CKA fails to show similarity there while ANC captures it (R7–R8).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: tested multilingual models and language pairs, including scaled MLMs and CLMs
reader_labels.reason: The reported trajectories show initial alignment followed by some renewed language specificity; the paper describes this pattern across the models and sizes studied (R10–R31).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: CKA indicates near-zero similarity, while other indexes and sentence matching indicate remaining similarity; the degree of apparent convergence depends on the measure (R1–R6).
